title: EIOPA's Financial Stability Report shows continued resilience in insurance amid geopolitical uncertainty and evolving structural risks
key_claim: EIOPA's June 2026 Financial Stability Report includes a deep dive on AI and says AI raises concerns about cyber risk, third-party dependencies, data governance and operational resilience for insurers.
frame_summary: EIOPA treats AI as an operational and cyber-resilience question for insurers' own use, alongside efficiency gains, rather than as a question about the cover insurers provide for others' AI.
verbatim_quote: While AI offers opportunities to improve efficiency across the insurance value chain, it also raises concerns about cyber risk, third-party dependencies, data governance and operational resilience.
notes: Structural anchor in the 3-6 month band (136 days). Press-release page read in the built-in browser 07/11/2026; the full report was not read.

title: The Insurance Industry’s Retreat from AI Threatens to Slow Innovation and Adoption
date_evidence: Report by Gregory C. Allen Published September 4, 2026 (meta citation_publication_date: Fri, 09/04/2026 - 12:00)
key_claim: CSIS argues insurance has become the de facto regulator of US AI deployment by withdrawal: carriers file endorsements stripping AI from policies, state commissioners have reportedly approved more than 80% of requests, and only 13 of 112 cells in a Geneva Association coverage matrix are available.
frame_summary: CSIS argues that insurers are regulating AI deployment by withdrawing cover rather than by setting affirmative standards, which turns insurance policy into de facto AI industrial policy.
verbatim_quote: Of 112 cells in the table, only 13 record an “Available” verdict and another 9 are “Limited.” The remaining 90 cells, roughly 80 percent of the matrix, are “Excluded.”
verbatim_list: State insurance commissioners have approved more than 80 percent of carrier requests to strip AI from those policies.
The carriers actively filing AI exclusions include Berkshire Hathaway, Chubb, Travelers, AIG, Tokio Marine Holdings, W.R. Berkley, Great American, and Fairfax Financial.
the company has stated that it has no current plans to implement the exclusion but has secured the regulatory option to do so.
OpenAI has secured cover of “up to $300 million” for emerging AI risks
Anthropic has agreed to pay a $1.5 billion settlement from its balance sheet
It is clear that CGL insurers do not currently model, underwrite, or price AI risks
for many, perhaps most, businesses, activities that cannot be insured are effectively prohibited.

title: The End of Silent AI Coverage: Exclusions Outrun Risk Transfer
key_claim: CSA's research note finds ISO's three generative AI exclusion endorsements are spreading into D&O, E&O and cyber lines, with Berkley's absolute exclusion and Beazley and QBE sublimits near 10% of cyber limits, and that underwriters willing to write affirmative AI cover converge on a common evidence bar.
frame_summary: CSA argues that silent AI cover is ending as exclusions spread beyond general liability faster than enterprises re-audit their coverage, and that documented controls are what buys affirmative cover.
verbatim_quote: Berkley has introduced an absolute AI exclusion across directors and officers (D&O), errors and omissions (E&O), and fiduciary liability products, while Beazley and QBE have introduced AI sublimits near 10% of overall cyber policy limits rather than excluding AI outright
verbatim_list: Since January 1, 2026, the Insurance Services Office (ISO) has circulated three generative-AI exclusion endorsements for commercial general liability policies (CG 40 47, CG 40 48, and CG 35 08)

a documented human override capability, a human-in-the-loop inventory of consequential AI decisions, data-provenance documentation, a named accountable executive, and deepfake-resistant authentication
notes: Research note from an industry security body; read in the built-in browser 07/11/2026.

frame_summary: Alston argues that NAIC regulators are moving from principles toward supervisory tools that test whether an insurer's own AI governance controls work in practice.

title: Insurer Interest in AI Coverage Exclusions Growing as Risk Becomes Omnipresent
key_claim: Insurance Journal reports carriers are increasingly filing with state regulators to use three ISO generative AI endorsements, that adoption will not be known until renewals, and that some insurers may price AI risk for extra premium instead of excluding it.
frame_summary: Insurance Journal frames the ISO exclusions as a fast-moving but still uncertain carrier response whose reach will be set by policyholder negotiation at renewal.
verbatim_quote: She has seen carriers increasingly submit filings with state insurance regulators to be able to use three ISO endorsements.
verbatim_list: But how widely they’re used may not be known for some time, at least until renewals start to come in.
choose to underwrite and price the risks probably for an additional premium rather than exclude them.
notes: Magazine feature quoting a Lathrop GPM partner and a Verisk vice president; read in the built-in browser 07/11/2026.

title: 7 Takeaways from the Big Data and Artificial Intelligence Working Group at the NAIC 2026 Summer National Meeting
